_comment: Voice-over lines for Bizzaro Bangalore. Generate with:
Two separate levers, per the pipeline notes: 'character' is fixed per
speaker and never changes between lines (that is the voice); 'delivery'
is per line (that is the take). Keeping them apart is what makes the
performance directable — without a delivery note every line in a scene
comes out in the same register regardless of what is happening in it.
Character descriptions deliberately say what NOT to do: left to itself
the model performs an accent rather than speaking in one.

narrator.character: a documentary narrator in the Vox explainer register — bright, articulate and conversational, speaking clean measured sentences with crisp consonants and a light forward momentum, as though walking the listener through evidence. He is dry rather than jokey, and trusts the material to be funny without selling it. Speak plainly and naturally — no announcer boom, no over-warm radio voice, no sing-song cadence, no theatrical emphasis, no caricature

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every day, thousands of auto rides begin in Bangalore. This is the story of the one that went right.
lines.delivery: matter-of-fact and unhurried, opening a case file; let the first sentence sit flat and ordinary, then land 'the one that went right' with a small dry lift — understated, never winking at the audience

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No pause. No haggling. He simply put the meter down.
lines.delivery: deadpan and clipped, almost flat; the first two fragments land like items being ticked off a list, then a small beat before the last clause, stated as plain fact rather than a punchline
